overview: The client status packet is a lifecycle signal: PERFORM_RESPAWN after death and OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT to open the statistics screen. Server-side anticheats use it in two ways. Respawn handling resets movement, inventory and combat state so the player starts clean after death, and a respawn command sent at the wrong time is a disabler signature. The open-inventory command also toggles the state that inventory-move and inv-tweak checks rely on, because moving while a screen is open is what inventory move cheats do.

checks.name: InventoryB (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Detects the open-inventory-achievement spam that inventory move and inventory tweak modules use to move while a screen is open.
checks.how_it_works: PacketCheck on WrappedPlayInClientCommand. When the command is OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT it sets the inventory flag; while the flag is set, if the player is attacking or swinging with less than 60 ms since the last flying packet, a buffer increments and fails at 3. Any flying packet clears the flag and refreshes lastFlying. The threshold of 3 keeps it tolerant of legitimate statistics-screen opens.
checks.detects: Inventory move, inventory tweak, and modules that keep the inventory state open while attacking.
checks.variations: CheaterDeleter InventoryMoveCheck keys the same state off the vanilla client-command listener; AutoEye InventoryWalk flags position changes while the inventory event is open.

checks.name: DisablerRespawn (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Flags PERFORM_RESPAWN commands sent while the player is not dead, the classic disabler that resets server-side state without dying.
checks.how_it_works: PacketHandler that reads GPacketPlayClientClientCommand. If the command is PERFORM_RESPAWN and the Bukkit player is not actually dead, a buffer increments and logs a violation at 3. Flying packets decay the buffer by 0.0125 per packet so lag does not accumulate it. The check annotation sets threshold 3.
checks.detects: Respawn disablers, respawn spam, and clients that send the respawn command to reset check state without a death.
checks.variations: NoCheatPlus validates respawn timing inside its moving checks; Frequency treats the packet only as inventory state; Grim resets its check state on the respawn flow instead of flagging.

checks.name: InventoryMoveCheck (CheaterDeleter)
checks.purpose: Flags movement while a container screen is open, using the vanilla client-command listener to track open state.
checks.how_it_works: Registers a ClientCommandC2SPacketListener plus movement, packet and damage listeners. While the player has a current screen handler open and changes position, it records the open time and inspects each move: upward movement with falling velocity, or horizontal acceleration in an axis where the server velocity is zero, flags Inventory Move. The first 500 ms after opening are ignored, damage resets the deltas, and closing the screen clears the open flag.
checks.detects: Inventory move, inventory walk and inv-tweak movement while a screen is open.
checks.variations: AutoEye InventoryWalk flags the same behavior with a one-line condition and reverts by closing the inventory; Frequency InventoryB catches the open-command spam itself; Photon InventoryMove runs on the open state from its own tracker.

checks.name: Respawn state reset (Grim)
checks.purpose: Rebuilds the simulation state when the respawn flow runs, so checks do not carry stale data across a death.
checks.how_it_works: PacketPlayerRespawn listens to the server-side respawn, join-game and health packets that follow the client's PERFORM_RESPAWN command. On UPDATE_HEALTH with health below zero it marks the self entity dead, and on RESPAWN it forces the player to accept a teleport before movements are processed, clears positions, resets ground, sneak, sprint and known-input state, resets several badpackets checks, and clears chunk and entity caches on a dimension change. The client half of the flow is the C16 PERFORM_RESPAWN command.
checks.detects: Not a flagging check; it prevents respawn-related desync and disablers that rely on stale check state.
checks.variations: Artemis DisablerRespawn flags premature respawn commands; NCP resets its move queue on respawn events inside the moving checks.

checks.name: InventoryWalk (AutoEye)
checks.purpose: Flags position changes while the inventory event is active and the client should be frozen.
checks.how_it_works: Check of type INVENTORY_EVENT: it fires when the client reports the open-inventory event. The check passes only if the player moved, lastFlying is zero, physics say the player is moving, the server velocity is zero on both horizontal axes, and less than 60 ms passed since the last move. On a pass it reverts by closing the player's inventory.
checks.detects: Inventory walk where the player moves while the inventory screen is open.
checks.variations: CheaterDeleter InventoryMoveCheck and Photon InventoryMove detect the same cheat with more tolerant timing; Frequency InventoryB catches the open-command spam that precedes it.
